thought.text: The build-3 log is missing. Let me check whether it started at all:

reasoning_content:
Interesting: the log file for build 3 doesn't exist, but the Gradle daemon and Kotlin daemon are running (started at 23:48, i.e., from my 23:49 build command... wait, the timestamps are 23:48/23:49 — this is the build I just started). The `nohup ... > /tmp/build_ni3.log` command: the log file doesn't exist?! And there's no flutter/fvm process either. Hmm — actually, the `cp` command was chained with `&&` and `;`: `cp ... && ls ... && export ... && cd /workspace && nohup fvm ... > log & echo pid`. Operator precedence: `A && B && C && D & echo` — this `&` applies to the entire list `A && B && C && D`! In other words, the whole chain was backgrounded, and `echo "build pid $!"` was printed immediately... The chain executed in the background, and the log should be created when nohup runs. But the log doesn't exist... However, the processes that started at 23:48-23:49 do exist.

Wait, looking again: the current time — the previous command ran around 23:52 (sleep 300 from around 23:49+23:51...). The daemon started at 23:40?? No: pid 8087 started at 23:40, CPU 23:12 — hmm, this is the daemon from build 2 (23:40). pid 9027's kotlin daemon started at 23:48.

So, where is the flutter process from build 3? The `nohup fvm flutter build apk` process isn't in the ps output (I grepped for "fvm|gradle|java" — fvm is a Go binary named fvm, and the flutter binary is a dart executable). My grep pattern "fvm|gradle|java" should match the "fvm" process. The fact that it's not found means the flutter build process died? But /tmp/build_ni3.log doesn't exist at all — meaning the redirect never happened...

Oh wait. I've got it — `nohup fvm flutter build apk ... > /tmp/build_ni3.log 2>&1 & echo "build pid $!"`. In the previous message, the command was:

```
cp /workspace/android/release.keystore /workspace/android/app/release.keystore && ls -la /workspace/android/app/release.keystore && export ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk && cd /workspace && nohup fvm flutter build apk --flavor ni ... > /tmp/build_ni3.log 2>&1 & echo "build pid $!"
```

The entire `cp && ls && export && cd && nohup fvm ...` is a single AND-list, and it's backgrounded by the `&` (the backgrounding of an AND-list). So everything ran in a background subshell. `echo` ran in the foreground. So the log should eventually appear (as soon as the subshell reaches the nohup line — immediately).

But the log doesn't exist, and there's no flutter process either. Strange. Maybe... the terminal tool kills background process groups when the command returns? Previously (builds 1 and 2), the same pattern survived — the log existed and the process ran. The difference: builds 1/2 were `export ... && cd ... && nohup ... & echo` — the same AND-list backgrounding! And they worked (the log was created).

Hmm, wait, did the build 3 subshell maybe die because cp's output... no, that's not it. Let me check the timestamps more carefully: the current time. build_ni2.log was last updated at 23:51 (build 2 ended at around 23:51). My keystore fix command was executed after that. The sleep 300 command ran after that. If the current time is about 23:56, the build 3 command was executed at around 23:52-23:53. The daemon 8087 started at 23:40 (build 2's daemon, still idle/alive). The kotlin daemon 9027 started at 23:48 (build 2). No new daemon for build 3 — consistent with build 3's gradle never having started (or it's reusing the existing daemon 8087! — the gradle daemon can be reused across builds, so there might be no new daemon process. It just connects to the existing one).

So, the flutter build process for build 3: `fvm` spawns `flutter` (dart). There's no flutter/dart process in the ps output. And there's no log file. Did the AND-list subshell fail early? For example, was `cp`'s target directory wrong? No, ls should have displayed it... The output of that command was only "build pid 9374" — because the entire chain was backgrounded, the output of cp/ls was never displayed even once (it went to the terminal's stdout, but was that lost? In the previous backgrounding, the output was lost in the same way — the build command only showed the pid).

Wait, actually, in the previous successful backgrounding, the same thing happened: only "build pid X" was shown. And the log file appeared. So this time the log didn't appear within 5 minutes + 1 minute. The subshell might be stuck at the `export`... no, that's not it.

Hold on — maybe the environment killed the background subshell when my next tool call started (the sleep 300 command). The previous builds survived similar gaps (build 1 survived my polling commands). Hmm.

Or: /tmp/build_ni3.log was created and then... /tmp was cleared? No, other logs remain.

Let me check once more: ls /tmp again now, and also ps for dart/flutter. And check the state of the workspace build directory for incremental progress (whether build/app/outputs exists).

action.command: date; ls -la /tmp/build_ni3.log 2>&1; ps aux | grep -E "dart|fvm" | grep -v grep | head -5; ls /workspace/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk 2>&1
